summary: Frontend-only verification of the new PhotoCropper modal. Login as chat_a → tab Profile → MODIFICA PROFILO works. The edit sheet renders with all required testIDs (photo-add-library, photo-add-camera, bio-input, profile-edit-save). App boots without any runtime JS errors related to PhotoCropper or expo-image-manipulator (bundle succeeds, imports resolve, no red screen). Bio-edit regression flow still works end-to-end. Two React Native deprecation warnings surfaced during the flow: `props.pointerEvents is deprecated` (originates from PhotoCropper.tsx circle-guide + grid Views) and `ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions has been deprecated` (profile.tsx pickPhoto). LIMITATION: expo-image-picker on the web preview does not expose a persistent <input type="file"> (patching HTMLInputElement.prototype.click captured 0 inputs, no input remains in DOM after invocation), so Playwright could not fire the actual OS file chooser and therefore could not open the cropper modal in-browser to exercise its interactive controls (zoom +/−, drag pan, checkmark upload) end-to-end from the UI. Per the review request this fallback path (JSX/testID + bootup + no import errors + edit-sheet reachable) was used and passed. Deprecated props.pointerEvents / MediaTypeOptions detected: see react_native_issues.

integration_issues.issue: Unable to trigger the cropper modal from Playwright on the Expo web preview: after clicking `photo-add-library` no <input type="file"> is left in the DOM (expo-image-picker web appears to create and dispose the input synchronously, and monkey-patching HTMLInputElement.click did not intercept any file inputs). Consequently zoom in/out at 4x/1x boundaries, drag-to-pan, cancel, and confirm-upload could NOT be exercised via the web UI. Component code, testIDs, and clamping logic look correct on static review, but should be validated on device (iOS/Android via Expo Go) or by adding a dev-only route/hook that renders PhotoCropper with a pre-set URI so it can be Playwright-tested on web.

react_native_issues.issue: `props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents` — the five `<View pointerEvents="none" ...>` occurrences (circleGuide + 4 grid lines) should move `pointerEvents` into the `style` object. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/PhotoCropper.tsx:248, 250-253
`ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions` has been deprecated. Use `ImagePicker.MediaType` (or an array of `ImagePicker.MediaType`) instead. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx:153

action_items: Replace `pointerEvents="none"` prop with `style={{ pointerEvents: 'none' }}` on the 5 overlay Views inside /app/frontend/src/components/PhotoCropper.tsx (lines 248, 250-253) to silence the RN deprecation warning.

Migrate `mediaTypes: ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions.Images` → `mediaTypes: ['images']` (or `ImagePicker.MediaType.Images` per the installed expo-image-picker version) in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx:153 to remove the ImagePicker deprecation warning.

(Optional / test-hardening) Expose a hidden dev-only route (e.g. `/dev/cropper`) that renders <PhotoCropper visible uri=… /> with a bundled sample image so future Playwright runs can validate zoom clamping, drag clamping, and confirm→upload without needing the native picker. This makes the feature testable on the web preview.

Perform on-device sanity check (Expo Go on real iOS/Android) for: (a) zoom-in disables at 4x, (b) zoom-out disables at 1x, (c) pan is clamped so no black margins appear around the image, (d) checkmark closes modal and adds a new 1:1 photo to the profile via POST /api/users/me/photos.
critical_code_review_comments: PhotoCropper clamping math looks correct: `maxTx/maxTy = max(0, (dispW/H - WINDOW)/2)` guarantees the image always covers the crop window, so the user cannot expose black bars. Reset-on-open effect (line 90-96) prevents stale tx/ty between different pictures.
Confirm() maps container→image pixels using the inverse of the same transform used for rendering — safe. Post-clamp on originX/Y/width/height (lines 169-172) is a good defensive net against rounding.

Cropper explicitly downscales to ≤1080px width before base64 encode, and profile.pickPhoto has a secondary 900px fallback (`payload.length > 900_000`) — good defensive layering against payload-too-large on POST /api/users/me/photos.
The busy state disables the confirm button and shows a spinner (line 219-224). Also `disabled={!ready || busy}` prevents double-submit. Good.
The `useEffect` clamping tx/ty on zoom change is correct but re-runs on every zoom step; harmless but could be memoised.

profile.tsx pickPhoto: setDetailsError(...) is called but the cropper modal is opened right after — if the picker was cancelled the modal is not opened (early return at line 162). If setDetailsError is set (e.g. photos ≥ 7) the cropper is also not opened. Flow is safe.

Missing catch on ImageManipulator.manipulateAsync inside confirm() only console.warns and keeps the modal open — the user has no visible feedback that the crop failed. Consider surfacing the error inline in the cropper header.

success_rate.frontend: 60% (bootup + testIDs + bio regression verified; interactive cropper flow unverifiable on web preview)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The web-preview cannot trigger expo-image-picker's OS file chooser via Playwright — after clicking [data-testid="photo-add-library"] no <input type="file"> is left in the DOM (verified by both querySelectorAll and by monkey-patching HTMLInputElement.prototype.click before the click, captured=0). Testing the actual cropper UI on web will require either (a) exposing a dev-only route that mounts <PhotoCropper visible uri=... />, or (b) testing on device / Expo Go. Login flow: switch to EMAIL tab, click text="Accedi" (lowercase, the mode-selector), fill email+password, then click text="ACCEDI" (uppercase, the red submit button) — both exist and are distinct. Profile tab is reached via `a[href*="profile"]` (no dedicated testID on the tab bar).
rca_of_issue: Not a bug — a testability limitation of expo-image-picker on the web target. The cropper component itself is statically correct and the two Italian strings ('RITAGLIA FOTO', 'Trascina la foto per scegliere la porzione visibile') plus all four testIDs are guaranteed by the JSX. Two RN deprecation warnings (pointerEvents prop, MediaTypeOptions) are the only concrete findings.
